source_question: Does every exact native access and each neighboring absolute target establish a complete scalar loader-zero owner, with an independent complete MOV/LEA/PUSH HIGHLOW anchor?
method: Read-only complete HIGHLOW relocation sweep over +/-16 RVA neighborhoods; every exact target fixup is disassembled using work/velocity_b/eng3_ranges/native_function_map.json intervals; exact address references are listed with instruction bytes and widths; nearby target RVAs are counted separately. Function map is used for instruction boundaries only.
classification: The module sweep inventories HIGHLOW fixup targets within plus/minus 16 RVAs of each requested cell and disassembles all exact-target fixups on the native instruction map. For every passing scalar, all memory accesses are base/index-free direct memory operands at the exact address and expected width. The only additional exact-target uses are PUSH-immediate address-taking references, recorded separately. Nearby targets are accounted separately; an interior access within a proposed extent is disqualifying.

anchor_selection.rule: One complete absolute-address MOV/LEA/PUSH instruction with exact HIGHLOW fixup, outside every assigned caller. Prefer an anchor outside work/velocity_b/blockers.json; where none exists, use a separate pending row outside this lane and mark it pending.
